-def basic_train(self, text, vocab_size, verbose):
+def regex_train_str(s, num_merges, stats, heap, merges, vocab, verbose):
+    # train_str over chunks separated by "\xff": pairs with it never count
+    # (earliest first occurrence in s == earliest chunk, then position)
+    stats_get = stats.get
+    for i in range(num_merges):
+        top, cands = pop_top_pairs(heap, stats_get, heappush, heappop)
+        if len(cands) == 1:
+            pair = cands[0]
+        else:
+            best = -1
+            for p in cands:
+                j = s.find(chr(p[0]) + chr(p[1]))
+                if best < 0 or j < best:
+                    best = j
+                    pair = p
+        idx = 256 + i
+        p0, p1 = pair
+        x = chr(idx)
+        s = s.replace(chr(p0) + chr(p1), x)
+        parts = s.split(x)
+        left = {}
+        _count_elements(left, map(_last, filter(None, parts[:-1])))
+        right = {}
+        _count_elements(right, map(_first, filter(None, parts[1:])))
+        left.pop("\xff", None)
+        right.pop("\xff", None)
+        stats[pair] -= len(parts) - 1
+        removed = [pair]
+        added = {}
+        for a, c in left.items():
+            a = ord(a)
+            p = (a, p0)
+            stats[p] -= c
+            removed.append(p)
+            added[(a, idx)] = c
+        for b, c in right.items():
+            b = ord(b)
+            p = (p1, b)
+            stats[p] -= c
+            removed.append(p)
+            added[(idx, b)] = c
+        c = parts[1:-1].count("")
+        if c:
+            stats[(p1, p0)] -= c
+            removed.append((p1, p0))
+            added[(idx, idx)] = c
+        for p in removed:
+            if stats_get(p) == 0:
+                del stats[p]
+        stats.update(added)
+        for p, c in added.items():
+            heappush(heap, (-c, p))
+        merges[pair] = idx
+        vocab[idx] = vocab[p0] + vocab[p1]
+        if verbose:
+            print(f"merge {i+1}/{num_merges}: {pair} -> {idx} ({vocab[idx]}) had {top} occurrences")
+
+
+def basic_train(self, text, vocab_size, verbose):

journal.text:
I tried replacing the per-chunk merge updates in minbpe/_train.py with a full-corpus approach for RegexTokenizer training: join all chunks with a 0xff separator and apply each merge with str.replace and split over the whole text. I added the new path near line 169 and later collapsed my earlier setup edit at lines 40-56 back to one line.

My sandbox evaluation built fine and gave identical outputs, but it was rejected. train_ir went from 311019829 to 336146877, ratio 1.0808, against a required 0.9900. encode_ir was unchanged at 380606937. I submitted no candidate.

What I believe now is that the existing code wins because it works on deduplicated chunks. Running replace and split over the non-deduplicated text costs more than the Python per-chunk updates it replaces. Setup-only tweaks I tried earlier land just under 1%.

Next time I should profile train_ir before editing, to find where the time actually goes in the merge loop. Any full-text rewrite should keep the deduplication.
